breaks.expected: A device with no signal never sends a grant-pull request: the pull must be gated on positive online evidence from this pass (e.g. a successful network round trip in the same pass, or a connectivity signal), not on 'zero failures' from a drain that did no network work.
breaks.observed: fetch is mocked to throw TypeError('Network request failed') (radio gone); outbox is empty so drainOutbox returns failed=0 without touching the network; the pass is classified clean and pullOfflineGrant() issues POST /v1/devices/register on every triggered pass (3 passes -> 3 register attempts), each failing as a transport error and inflating consecutiveFailures. The only 'online' evidence the runtime consults is the anchored trusted-time reading, which stays anchored while the app is foregrounded regardless of connectivity. Fix (all inside write_paths): (1) new apps/mobile/src/data/installationKey.ts — Keychain-only per-installation id via react-native-keychain (service com.picklesensei.offline.installation-key, AFTER_FIRST_UNLOCK_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY, same lazy/fail-soft/bounded pattern as sessionVault.ts), generated once as `ios-<uuid>`, validated against ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,127}$, read-back confirmed so only what the Keychain holds is the identity, concurrent readers share one in-flight read; never SQLite/AsyncStorage. (2) offlineCapabilities.ts — pure `offlineGrantPullNeeded(wallet)`: true only when no receipt is pending and every grant is expired or an active free grant with remaining=0 (reconcile_required = unproven time → no pull). (3) syncRuntime.ts — after a CLEAN pass (outbox drained with 0 failures, no pending journal recovery, 0 pending receipts) under an `anchored`, non-rollback trusted-time reading, with generation/owner fencing before each request: registerDevice (idempotent, attestation env from __DEV__) then requestOfflineGrant with requestedTickets 2 (free) / 0 (canonicalAccess.premium) → holdOfflineGrant. Definitive 4xx refusals (excluding 401/408/429) are recorded once under an access-snapshot key and not retried until canonicalAccess changes; transport failures (5xx/401/408/429/network) increment consecutiveFailures and follow the ordinary sync backoff. Nothing spends, releases or reclaims. Commits: 17a02158 (test only, separately), 560450b6 (implementation). Pushed; no PR opened. non_blocking_issues: INFERRED (apps/mobile/src/data/syncRuntime.ts:165 + trustedTime.ts:714-760): the online signal is `anchored` trusted time, which only api.ts `request()` sets after an authenticated response with a Date header. Callers of `request()` are the outbox transport, permit client, offline-grant client, release-policy client and feedback — nothing that runs on an idle launch (accessApi/progress do not feed observeServerTime). So a fresh install that signs in and idles will not pull its first grant until the user's first online rating anchors time (the pull then happens on the following pass, ~30 s). Consistent with the frozen wording ('trusted-time reading available') and with evaluateLease (grants cannot execute without an anchored reading anyway), so not blocking; a follow-up package could anchor time from an existing authenticated launch request.

INFERRED (syncRuntime.ts:165-190): an anchor established earlier in the process stays `anchored` after the device loses connectivity; with an empty outbox the pass is clean and the pull will attempt registerDevice once, fail with a network error, return 'failed' and back off (consecutiveFailures++). No state changes and nothing is held, so allocation invariants are preserved; the repo has no connectivity abstraction to gate on. Tested offline case (failed outbox row) covers the common path.

INFERRED (syncRuntime.ts:65-77, 168-170): a refusal recorded while canonicalAccess is null is keyed 'unknown' and released as soon as access loads; a refusal such as offline.device_not_attested (server-side attestation policy, p_attested=false registration) stays suppressed until any canonicalAccess field changes — matches the frozen 'not retried until access changes' rule but a persistent server-side refusal is only re-tried when access mutates or the runtime is reconfigured (new generation).
